record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: For binary patterns p in abelian pattern avoidance for partial words, improve the known sufficient length bound: the source states that if the length of p is at least 360, then there exists a binary partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense. What smaller bound, if any, can replace 360 while preserving that conclusion?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A partial word over a finite alphabet A is a sequence whose letters belong to A together with a special symbol ⋄ (called a hole) that is regarded as "undefined" and is compatible with every letter of A. Two full words u, v over A of the same length are abelian equivalent (written u ~_ab v) if v is a permutation of the letters of u, equivalently if for every a ∈ A the number of occurrences of a in u equals the number of occurrences of a in v. A pattern is a nonempty word p over a pattern alphabet E = {x_1, x_2, …} of variables. A partial word w over A is said to meet the pattern p in the abelian sense if there exists a non-erasing morphism-like assignment that replaces each occurrence of a variable x_i in p by a factor of w in such a way that the resulting consecutive factors of w are pairwise abelian-equivalent whenever the corresponding variables are equal (and the holes ⋄ in w are treated as wildcards compatible with this equivalence). Otherwise, w avoids p in the abelian sense. A pattern p is called binary if it uses exactly two distinct variables.

Known bound. It is known that for every binary pattern p of length at least 360, there exists an infinite binary partial word containing infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense.

Problem. Determine the smallest integer N (or improve the value 360 as much as possible) such that the following statement still holds: for every binary pattern p of length at least N, there exists an infinite binary partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense.
artifact.status_search_result: Search located the original result establishing the length-360 sufficient bound for abelian avoidance of binary patterns by binary partial words with infinitely many holes (Blanchet-Sadri et al., RAIRO ITA 2014). Subsequent improvements for full words (e.g., every binary pattern of length > 14 is abelian-2-avoidable, MFCS 2016) do not address the partial-word setting with infinitely many holes. No source was found that explicitly improves the 360 bound in the partial-word setting, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Abelian pattern avoidance in partial words
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that binary patterns of length at least 360 are abelian avoidable by binary partial words with infinitely many holes.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the original 360 bound cited in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Every Binary Pattern of Length Greater Than 14 Is Abelian-2-Avoidable
status_evidence.snippet: Every binary pattern of length greater than 14 is abelian-2-avoidable (in full words).
status_evidence.claim: Improves abelian-2-avoidability bounds for full words but not in the partial-words-with-infinitely-many-holes setting.
